newsitem.title: UK: Dlr firm in late Europe, dlr/mark at 10-day high.
newsitem.headline: Dlr firm in late Europe, dlr/mark at 10-day high.

text.p: The dollar continued to probe recent highs over the European afternoon with strong U.S. GDP data and a buoyant start on Wall Street helping dollar/mark to 1.7372 marks -- its highest level since June 17.
The U.S. Commerce Department earlier announced that GDP had risen a revised 5.9 percent in the first quarter, marking the economy's most robust performance in nearly nine years.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average celebrated the news with a 60 point opening rally and the optimism pushed dollar-yen to a European high of 114.61. But economists doubt the dollar has the legs to maintain this run and see the upside capped at 115.00.

"The Japanese authorities would like to see dollar/yen stable and the U.S. authorities won't want the dollar to get too high...at levels above 115.00 it will start to look difficult," said Adrian Schmidt at Chase Investment Bank.

The dollar has soared well over a yen to 114.63 in the past day. Schmidt saw no conclusive explanations for the rally, but felt short-covering following the release of subdued Japanese economic data was the most likely cause.
Dollar/mark's progress to a 10-day high was coloured by the mark's torrid performance against sterling -- presently at a 59-month low -- and general concern over EMS currencies.
"We feel that the dollar will continue to rise against EMS currencies on the basis of ongoing concern over Emu," said Robert Hayward at Bank of America.
The dollar -- backed by a positive outlook for the economy that was amply confirmed by the GDP report -- is sitting pretty, whereas the EMS currencies look prone to any number of upsets.

"Sentiment towards the EMS units is extremely vulnerable to changes in tone and direction over EMU and these could crop up almost anywhere," said one London dealer. Dlr/mark gains made this clear, but the way ahead looks capped, with the dollar facing a stiff test at 1.7400, he said.
"Dlr/mark is rangebound and and I can see no grounds for a break from the recent highs or lows," he said.
Chase's Schmidt saw dollar/mark trapped within 171.00-174.20, with the upside target presenting an area of major resistance.

This might be tested on Thursday if U.S. payrolls data reinforced the message of an economy in full flush. But coming just after the FOMC meeting, it would have to be accompanied by evidence of strengthening demand if it was to prompt a Fed tightening, he said.
The Federal Open Markets Committee meets July 1 and 2 but is not expected to usher in higher U.S. rates.
"It would be a huge shock if the FOMC meeting led to anything," said Bank of America's Hayward.
Greenspan has been careful to flag moves in advance, and while further rates hikes may be in store for the coming months, the market was of a mind that there would be no move soon.
"The biase is towards tightening -- at a future date -- if economic strength persists," said Hayward.
